lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
- Cut the signal's daily turnover from 34% to 21% with a cost-aware position smoother, keeping 90% of gross returns and lowering estimated slippage by a third.
- Confirmed the forecast gain over the nested HAR-RV baseline with standard Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices.
- Joining 120 microstructure features point-in-time across six venues, deduplicating late prints and versioning each schema, built a feature store the team reused in two later projects.
- Annualized the signal's daily Sharpe ratio by multiplying it by 252 before reporting it to the desk.
- Documented the backtest assumptions, transaction-cost model and known failure regimes in the desk's research wiki, which the next intern cohort used to onboard in their first week.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Built the lab's simulation pipeline on the shared cluster, cutting a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours, with every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.

- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation while maintaining the lab's shared cluster, organizing the weekly reading group and grading for two courses, which was downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Cut forecast error from 0.20 to 0.15, a 33% improvement, by adding realized-volatility features and an asymmetric loss.
- Improved the model's directional hit rate by 6% on 30 equity indices, from 52% to 58%, with a temporal convolutional model.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Placed 41st of 2,900 teams with a gradient-boosting ensemble on 300 engineered features, finishing in the top 2% of the private leaderboard.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Wrote the team's feature-selection script using permutation importance, trimming 900 candidate features to 300 without losing validation score.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Quantitative experience should appear before the bakery role.
items.because: The current first role signals retail operations and delays the strongest evidence.

items.says: Research, quantitative experience, and additional employment should be visibly separated.
items.because: The current structure makes the résumé appear less targeted.

items.says: The résumé lacks a concise summary or research-focus section.
items.because: The reader must infer the intended career path from disconnected academic, finance, retail, and competition experience.

items.says: A Publications or Selected Research section is missing.
items.because: The main JASA research output is buried inside an old job bullet.

items.says: The dates leave an apparent gap in research activity after August 2021 if the lab work continued into the Ph.D.
items.because: The old assistantship otherwise appears disconnected from the current doctorate.

items.says: The volatility project reports several favorable views of what appears to be the same experiment.
items.because: The redundancy may look like opportunistic metric selection rather than distinct capabilities.

items.says: The Kaggle entry may deserve less space than research publications or quant work if it is not directly relevant.
items.because: Research output is more important for the target roles.

items.says: Punctuation, date formatting, and capitalization should be standardized.
Placeholder contact details should be replaced if they are not intentionally anonymized.
items.because: The current domain and phone number look fictional and could damage credibility.

items.says: The code link should lead directly to a useful profile or repository collection.
items.because: Reviewers should be able to inspect the volatility study, packages, or reproducible research easily.

items.says: A LinkedIn link could be added if the profile is complete and professional.
A location could be added when relevant to the targeted roles.
The Ph.D. entry does not identify the research area, dissertation focus, advisor, or selected topic.
items.because: A quant reviewer needs to understand what the doctorate studies.

items.says: The bachelor’s degree should have less visual prominence than the Ph.D.
items.because: The doctorate and research output are much more relevant.

items.says: This management bullet could be shortened or omitted for a quant application.
items.because: It has little relevance to quantitative research and is weaker than the quantified bakery accomplishment.

items.says: “Labour” should use spelling consistent with a résumé targeting US employers.
items.because: The rest of the résumé uses US conventions.

items.says: The bullet lacks a substantiated business metric such as budget size or operational volume.
items.because: Its value is managerial responsibility rather than technical qualification.

items.says: The time period for the reduction in unsold bread is not stated.
The bullet does not establish whether the reduction was primarily attributable to the candidate’s process.
items.because: The causal wording needs substantiation.

items.says: The internship heading lacks safe-to-disclose desk, asset-class, or strategy context.
items.because: This is the most directly relevant employer on the résumé.

items.says: The entry does not say whether the work was research-only, paper-traded, or deployed.
items.because: The status of the reported results affects their credibility.

items.says: The 1.1-to-1.5 Sharpe change is unclear about whether it describes the full desk portfolio, an incremental strategy, or a simulated combination.
items.because: Reviewers need to understand how the signal produced the improvement.

items.says: The exact backtest period and evaluation protocol are under-specified.
items.because: The claim needs methodological context to be credible.

items.says: The bullet does not clearly distinguish simulated performance from live performance.
items.because: An out-of-sample backtest should not imply deployed results.

items.says: “Raised the desk book’s Sharpe ratio” may overstate attribution if the signal was not incorporated into the actual desk book.
items.because: The wording can imply a change in actual desk performance.

items.says: The annualization convention for the reported Sharpe ratios is not stated.
items.because: Quant reviewers will want to know how the figures were annualized.

items.says: “Keeping 90% of gross returns” is not defined precisely.
items.because: It is unclear whether this means original gross return, net return, or performance after smoothing.

items.says: The slippage reduction is not clearly identified as model-estimated or observed in execution.
items.because: The result is model-dependent if it was only estimated.

items.says: The turnover, return, and slippage metrics are not shown to use consistent periods and measurement conventions.
items.because: Their relationships are not fully clear.

items.says: “Standard” is too vague a description of the Diebold–Mariano tests.
items.because: Naming the test alone does not demonstrate statistical rigor.

items.says: “Confirmed” is stronger than the stated evidence may support.
items.because: The presence of Diebold–Mariano tests alone does not establish robustness.

items.says: The bullet omits the significance level or proportion of indices showing significance.
items.because: A compact indicator of the statistical result is needed.

items.says: The special treatment required by the nested comparison is not explained.
items.because: The meaning of “nested” in the test setup is unclear.

items.says: The bullet does not address multiple comparisons across 30 indices.
items.because: Testing many datasets can affect the interpretation of significance.

items.says: “Joining” is the wrong word or an unfinished edit.
items.because: It makes the sentence grammatically broken and difficult to parse.

items.says: The data-engineering actions and the feature-store outcome should be separated more clearly.
items.because: The technical contribution is compressed and loses impact.

items.says: The specific data-integration task is unclear.
items.because: The bullet should explain what was joined across the six venues.

items.says: The point-in-time methodology and leakage-control constraint are not explained.
items.because: The bullet should show how look-ahead leakage was prevented.

items.says: The schema-versioning contribution is under-specified.
items.because: The reviewer cannot tell what versioning work was performed.

items.says: The candidate’s personal contribution to building the feature store is not sufficiently clear.
items.because: The bullet should distinguish what was personally built.

items.says: The technology used for the feature store is not named.
items.because: Naming it would make the engineering contribution more concrete.

items.says: The daily Sharpe ratio is annualized incorrectly by multiplying it by 252.
items.because: For independently distributed daily returns, annualization generally uses the square root of the number of periods.

items.says: The first-week onboarding result is not identified as measured or informally observed.
items.because: The basis for the outcome is unclear.

items.says: The title and dates make the research role look like an old assistantship disconnected from the current Ph.D.
items.because: The entry contains some of the résumé’s strongest research evidence.

items.says: The bullet does not name the relevant tooling or workflow.
items.because: Technical implementation details would strengthen the research-engineering result.

items.says: The source of the Monte Carlo speedup is not explained.
items.because: It is unclear whether the gain came from parallelization, algorithmic changes, scheduling, or another intervention.

items.says: The paper title is missing.
items.because: The paper should not be identifiable only through a job bullet.

items.says: The candidate’s authorship position is not stated.
items.because: “My proof” does not precisely establish authorship.

items.says: The paper’s submission status should be stated more precisely.
items.because: “Under review at JASA” is meaningful only when presented exactly.

items.says: A paper or preprint link is missing if one is available.
items.because: Reviewers should be able to inspect the research output.

items.says: The first-person phrase “my proof” is inconsistent with the résumé’s otherwise implicit style.
items.because: The wording should remain stylistically consistent.

items.says: The teaching bullet could be shortened or omitted for industry applications.
items.because: It is less important than the research, modeling, and engineering evidence for a quant role.

items.says: The 4.8/5 rating is not identified as coming from formal student evaluations.
items.because: The provenance of the rating is unclear.

items.says: The bullet combines software publication, systems administration, academic service, and teaching support.
items.because: The unrelated duties make the main package accomplishment difficult to identify.

items.says: The R package lacks a direct link.
items.because: The open-source software should be easy for reviewers to inspect.

items.says: The meaning of 3,000 downloads is not defined.
items.because: It could refer to package downloads, repository downloads, or another measure.

items.says: The project is not clearly distinguished from the Northpeak work.
items.because: Its relationship to the broader research profile is unclear.

items.says: The project lacks a repository or paper link if one is available.
items.because: The “Independent Research” label alone does not establish rigor or reproducibility.

items.says: It is unclear whether the project is Ph.D. research, independent work, or a portfolio project.
items.because: The current label does not explain its relationship to the candidate’s research.

items.says: The ongoing entry does not distinguish completed work from work still under development.
items.because: The project is dated “Present.”

items.says: The time-split or walk-forward validation design is not stated.
items.because: The out-of-sample claim depends on rigorous, leakage-free validation.

items.says: The 7% improvement is not identified as an average, median, or aggregate result.
items.because: Its interpretation across 30 indices is unclear.

items.says: The bullet does not confirm that the baseline and model use identical information sets.
items.because: A fair comparison requires the same available information.

items.says: The sample period is missing.
items.because: It may be important for interpreting the result.

items.says: A reduction from 0.20 to 0.15 is 25%, not 33%, relative to 0.20.
items.because: The stated percentage overstates the improvement.

items.says: “Forecast error” is not defined precisely.
items.because: Generic forecast error is not interchangeable with QLIKE.

items.says: This result is redundant unless it measures a materially different outcome from the QLIKE result.
items.because: The need for another metric is not explained.

items.says: The change from 52% to 58% is six percentage points, not necessarily 6%.
items.because: Percent and percentage-point increases are different.

items.says: Directional accuracy should be removed or consolidated unless it is a central evaluation criterion.
items.because: Its relevance to the stated forecasting objective is not explained.

items.says: The hit-rate result lacks statistical uncertainty or a benchmark.
items.because: The metric needs context to be meaningful.

items.says: The bullet repeats the same model, dataset, and “30 indices” wording without adding a distinct contribution.
items.because: The repetition makes the project look metric-heavy rather than methodologically rigorous.

items.says: The competition is not named.
items.because: A recognizable competition name would give the result more credibility.

items.says: The competition domain or dataset type is missing.
items.because: The reader lacks context for the project.

items.says: The candidate’s individual contribution to the ensemble and feature engineering is unclear.
items.because: A team result should not imply sole ownership.

items.says: The top-2% percentile calculation should be verified.
The original leakage mechanism is not explained.
items.because: The bullet should demonstrate understanding of temporal leakage.

items.says: The metric represented by the 0.02 gap is not identified.
items.because: The numerical result cannot otherwise be interpreted.

items.says: It is unclear whether closing the gap improved generalization or merely reduced optimistic validation.
items.because: Those outcomes have different meanings.

items.says: The bullet does not explain whether permutation importance and feature selection were computed within each training fold.
items.because: Feature selection can leak information when performed outside the validation loop.

items.says: It is not stated whether the selected features were used for the final private-leaderboard submission.
items.because: The connection to the competition result is unclear.

items.says: Programming languages, frameworks, and infrastructure tools should be categorized separately.
items.because: Python and R are languages, while PyTorch and Kafka are different kinds of tools.

items.says: Kafka appears without supporting evidence elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: Unsupported skills can look like keyword padding.

items.says: The skills section does not show relevant version-control, database, Linux, distributed-computing, or numerical tools if they were genuinely used.
items.because: Those tools would better support the research-infrastructure evidence.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: A technical reviewer will notice a typo in a field central to the finance bullets.

items.says: The methods list underrepresents the candidate’s technical breadth.
items.because: It omits supported areas such as volatility forecasting, microstructure modeling, statistical testing, Monte Carlo simulation, sparse regression, and covariance estimation.

items.says: The most relevant quantitative-finance methods should appear first.
items.because: The current list omits recognizable domain terms from the experience.
